cards.title: The camera row (keys and attention)

aliases.name: The attention law
aliases.source: CAPABILITIES[The camera arrival: the eye goes to the landed card]

cards.does: A scene's own camera: authored keys zoom and pan one persistent 2D similarity between key times on a named ease, or the attention law leans the frame toward each landed card; with neither the camera stays locked.
cards.when: the stage is wider than the frame, or a move is tied to a landing (E51) - never a drift on a held chart; locked is the default

author.key: shot row 8th element {'keys': [{t, s, look, ease}], 'attention': 'locked' | 'landings'} (validate_camera / validate_camera_row)

phases.name: lean in
phases.does: with attention=landings the camera leans toward the landed card

phases.name: hold
phases.does: held while the card is up

phases.name: release
phases.does: eases back to identity before the card leaves

options.means: Camera ease: cubic: A camera key eases in by a cubic ease-out (the default).
Camera ease: hold: The previous key holds, then the camera steps to this key at its t.
Camera ease: inout: A camera key eases in and out symmetrically.
The attention pull: When a dock lands the camera leans 1.06 toward it from the contact frame, holds while the card is up, and releases before it leaves.
Camera ease: linear: A camera key travels at constant speed.
The locked camera: The camera never moves on its own; with no keys it is the identity.
On a full-stage page: refuse (default) names a key or landing pull that would cut the title, y ticks, source or a measured tag; clamp stops the pull at the reach (landing_zoom).

lives.note: no T1 row of its own: six rows (the four eases, the two attentions) named camera:keys as their parent

callable.why: the locked default runs on every build; keys and landings used only on the Tokyo test bed

cards.title: The pedestal: the camera drops through the stage once, after the build

aliases.name: Pedestal (don't: a camera move over a build, M14)

cards.does: The camera stands raised by `by` of the stage's height - the page's lower part below the frame - until its word, then travels straight down to the identity over `dur` and holds there, locked.
cards.when: the stage is taller than the frame and the hidden part is below (the iceberg's base under the waterline) - one move, after the build has settled; never over a build (M14)

author.key: shot row 8th element {'pedestal': {at, dur, by, ease?}} (validate_camera's _validate_pedestal; pedestal_errors: M14 and the row's span)

phases.name: raised
phases.does: until `at` the camera looks `by` of the stage's height above the centre: the world sits that much lower on screen

phases.name: down
phases.does: straight down to the identity on the in-out ease (rest to rest)

phases.name: held
phases.does: the identity: every frame after is the locked camera's

blends.source: Bravos harvest v2 A33 (BUB 0:00-0:48): the tip, then the camera drops past the waterline to the base
blends.became: the raised opening and the one move down; BUB measured ~0.21 H of travel, then still

options.means: `ease: cubic|inout|linear` (absent = inout); `hold` is refused - a step is a cut.
no key (P72 T53 (a)): on a pedestal row the ledger world wears its page's ground, carried up by `by` - the raised frame opens on the page's own sky, never the stage's void.
